title: Valuation, Tax & Transaction Costs
intro: The rules that convert a sale price into net proceeds, and the market evidence that brackets what a buyer would pay. California and Los Angeles both tax the transfer, and federal law taxes the gain — so the headline price is not the number that matters.

rows.metric: General ad valorem levy
rows.display: 1% of assessed value ($4 per $100 at a 25% assessment ratio)
rows.note: Revenue and Taxation Code §93(b) implements Article XIII A. Voter-approved bond levies sit on top.

rows.metric: Annual cap on assessed-value growth
rows.note: RTC §51(a)(1)(D): the annual inflation factor 'in no event shall ... exceed 2 percent'. The base-year value generally resets on a change of ownership — the core of Proposition 13.

rows.metric: Taxable value rule
rows.display: Lesser of (base-year value × inflation factor) or full cash value
rows.note: This is why a long-held asset can carry a tax bill far below 1% of market value, and why a sale resets the buyer's basis and tax.

rows.metric: Relief for value decline or disaster damage
rows.display: Decline-in-value (Prop 8) and disaster relief applications available
rows.note: Los Angeles County Assessor accepts decline-in-value applications for the 2026-27 tax year from 2026-07-02, deadline 2026-11-30.

rows.metric: City of Los Angeles real property transfer tax (base)
Measure ULA additional tax, $5.4M to under $10.9M
rows.note: Thresholds are indexed annually to Chained CPI. These are the amounts in force for closings after 30 June 2026.

rows.metric: Measure ULA additional tax, $10.9M and above
rows.note: A $10.9M sale therefore pays $648,550 in city transfer tax alone before any county documentary transfer tax.

rows.metric: Measure ULA effective date
Depreciation recovery period, nonresidential real property
rows.note: Land is not depreciable. Bonus depreciation does not apply to the building because it is limited to 20-year-or-shorter property.

rows.metric: Unrecaptured section 1250 gain
rows.note: This is the depreciation you already deducted coming back on sale — and it is why an exchanged basis matters.

rows.metric: Top long-term capital gains rate
rows.note: 15% applies to most taxpayers; 20% above the high-income thresholds.

rows.metric: Net investment income tax
rows.display: May apply to investment income above statutory thresholds
rows.note: Topic 409 refers to Topic 559. The 3.8% rate itself was not read from an IRS page in this pass, so it is not asserted as verified.

rows.metric: Section 1031 like-kind exchange
rows.display: Gain not recognised when real property is exchanged solely for like-kind real property held for business or investment
rows.note: Since 2018 §1031 applies to real property only. Deferral is not forgiveness: the old basis carries into the replacement property.

rows.metric: Diversified net-lease acquisition cash yield, 2025
rows.note: Realty Income Corp., FY2025 Form 10-K / earnings release (filed 2026-02-24). Read from the SEC filing summary; the exhibit itself was not line-by-line verified in this pass. This is the benchmark yield for the 'sell and redeploy' strategy.

rows.metric: Diversified net-lease same-store rental revenue growth, 2025
rows.note: Same source as VL-14. Growth is materially lower than a 2.5% contract escalator — that is the trade-off for the higher yield.

rows.metric: Single-tenant QSR cap rate for PARCEL-01
rows.note: No government publisher produces single-asset cap rates, and this project used no paid data. The model's 6.0% going-in cap is an explicit assumption anchored to the 4.84% 10-year Treasury plus 110–215 bp, cross-checked against 7.0–7.3% diversified net-lease yields. A broker opinion of value is required to replace it.

rows.metric: Comparable rents for a central-LA QSR box
rows.note: Not available from any official source. Rent is therefore modelled only via escalators and market-reset ratios, never as a dollar figure.

rows.metric: Effective all-in property tax rate (1% plus bonds and assessments)
rows.note: Secondary sources put typical LA County effective rates at roughly 1.1%–1.25%. Not verified against a Tax Rate Area book in this pass; the model uses the statutory 1% only and therefore understates the owner's cost slightly.

rows.metric: Cap-rate spread: model going-in cap less 10-year Treasury
rows.note: A thin risk premium by historical standards. If long rates keep rising, this spread has room to widen — which means values have room to fall.

rows.metric: Yield gap: diversified net-lease cash yield less PARCEL-01 going-in cap
rows.note: This spread, not the absolute level of rates, is what makes selling and redeploying accretive on day one. It is also the model assumption most worth challenging.
